parallel.requirements: Recognized the required Rust 2021, std-only, byte-for-byte compatible port with root test20.rs, Cargo project files, argument parsing, float formatting, default colors, conversions, and oracle-based verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent assigned one child as the implementation owner for /output and another read-only child as behavior analyst. Parent expected to inspect both after the swarm returned and resume the coder if needed.
parallel.implementation: Implementation child wrote the Cargo project and modules, compiled with cargo and rustc, matched base examples, built fuzz harnesses, and continued investigating saturation/hue edge mismatches. Analyst child generated a behavior spec and /tmp/golden corpus.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Only the implementation child wrote the deliverable tree under /output. The analyst wrote /tmp/golden and returned text; no parent post-processing occurred before cancellation. Artifact validation later copied Cargo.toml, test20.rs, src modules, and target/release/test20.
parallel.verification: Implementation child confirmed six base cases and performed randomized comparisons with mismatches during local search. Analyst verified behavior categories and corpus exits. Official evaluator later passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Parallel process timed out with the implementation child aborted and no final child handoff or parent inspection of the completed analyst report, although the saved artifact passed the official evaluator.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, byte-for-byte conversion task, Cargo layout, root test20.rs, exact CLI parsing and float output needs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned exploration, implementation, compilation, fuzzing, binary disassembly checks, and deliverable placement without delegation or child handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: Serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, color modules, cfmt.rs, and test20.rs, fixed an import, iterated on formatter and color formulas, then inspected disassembly to identify exact hue and conversion operation order.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All implementation and probing occurred in one local trajectory, with no cross-agent integration. Artifact validation later copied test20, Cargo.toml, test20.rs, cfmt.rs, and color modules.
serial.verification: Serial run compiled, matched documented examples, fuzzed against the C++ oracle, examined failing cases, and used objdump to resolve exact C++ operation orders. Official evaluator later passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process also timed out before a final user-facing response, but because there were no child agents, no completed child result or implementation handoff was trapped.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the complete C++ to Rust migration requirements and included them in the implementation child brief.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and recognized the same byte-for-byte output, std-only, project layout, and black-box constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition difference explains the official outcome; both passed 40/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the task into an implementation child and a read-only behavior analyst child, with the parent planning a later follow-up pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in one actor and used local todos for implementation, build, example verification, and fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child lifecycle and monitoring boundaries; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent supplied detailed implementation and analysis briefs, but the behavior analyst's output was only returned through the aggregate swarm result after the parent had waited to timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial actor kept the discovered behavior, fuzz failures, and disassembly findings in the same context where implementation decisions were made.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a result-transfer timing boundary; serial consumed its own findings directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implementation child wrote the Rust files early, compiled successfully, and then spent many steps refining edge-case float behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a separate Rust layout, fixed compile errors, and used objdump/disassembly to resolve exact color conversion operation order.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the necessary behavior, but parallel implementation work was isolated in an aborted child while serial implementation state stayed local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Analyst child completed and implementer child remained active; the parent got an aggregate result only after cancellation, showing one completed child and one aborted child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the single actor was itself cancelled at the outer deadline after doing local work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a usable child-result decision point; serial had no child result to join or inspect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the implementation child wrote the deliverable tree, while the analyst was instructed not to modify /output and wrote support data under /tmp/golden.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote its own deliverable tree in /output without concurrent writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision explains the outcome; parallel shared-state risk did not materialize into artifact failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implementation child matched base cases and found fuzz mismatches during its search; the official evaluator later passed the saved artifact 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial matched examples, fuzzed, used disassembly to resolve edge differences, and the official evaluator also passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Official acceptance is equal; serial has more visible local reverse-engineering closure, while parallel's official pass comes despite child cancellation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 44 LLM requests, two subagents, and timed out; the parent saw the swarm result only after cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 41 LLM requests, no subagents, and also timed out at the outer process after local work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted process time, but only parallel had a blocking child wait with one completed result and one aborted child.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed: parallel 40/40 and serial 40/40. The difference is not outcome quality but process shape. Parallel delegated implementation and behavior analysis, then waited on the aggregate swarm until the deadline, receiving the analyst report only in the terminal result while the implementer was aborted. Serial performed the equivalent investigation and implementation locally, so there was no child handoff to monitor or consume.
parallel_contributors: Two-child decomposition separated implementation from behavior probing.
Blocking swarm result delayed parent inspection of completed analyst findings until terminal cancellation.
serial_contributors: Single actor kept probing, implementation, fuzzing, and disassembly findings in one context.
No child result lifecycle or cross-agent handoff was involved.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs spent substantial effort on ordinary numeric-formatting and f32 operation-order issues.
Parallel's local fuzz mismatches during search are implementation-debugging evidence, not proof of final official failure.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a supported parallel process consequence, not a cause of failure

candidates.reason: Implementation was explicitly assigned to agent-0, which wrote the Rust project and compiled it.
There were not multiple independently implemented components requiring an unowned integration step.
The implementation child owned the deliverable project and artifact validation found the expected root test20.rs and build outputs.
The parent and implementation child covered implementation, build, verification, and delivery; the issue was timeout monitoring, not an unowned end-to-end pipeline.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the coder and analyst ran concurrently.
Exploration did not complete as a first phase before implementation; the implementation child wrote and tested while the analyst probed.
The critical implementation path had an assigned child and produced an accepted artifact; the directly evidenced boundary is the parent's blind aggregate wait.
Two children are not excessive fan-out, there were no retry waves, and the timeout chain is more specifically captured by parent monitoring.
Although agent-0 had the full implementation scope, it produced a working deliverable; the unfinished final handoff is part of the wait/cancel lifecycle rather than an oversized allocation label.
The implementation and analyst briefs included task behavior, output layout, acceptance checks, and verification requirements; no known requirement was omitted from a child brief.

The agents did not produce incompatible interdependent components; the analyst supplied support information and the coder wrote the deliverable. The failure mode is timing of the aggregate result, not an absent interface contract.
No known finding is shown to disappear through summary or transfer; the analyst's behavior spec appears intact in the terminal swarm result.
The analyst handoff is long, but there was no post-return decision window in which its volume prevented reduction; the issue is that it arrived only at terminal cancellation.
No actor consumed a handoff describing superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parent did not make a final whole-task completion claim before closure; official evaluator success cannot create this label.
No replacement child or retry episode is present.

candidates.reason: Agent-0 was cancelled, but that cancellation is the terminal symptom of the same blocking parent wait; Blind Timeout Wait is the more direct correctable boundary for this episode.
A deliverable tree already existed in /output and was copied/evaluated successfully; no complete candidate was left unpromoted or unplaced.
No child implementation was merged only after integrated verification without a post-merge check.
The delegated implementation was written directly into /output and became the evaluated artifact; missing final child text is not a separate unjoined implementation episode.
The completed analyst result was returned in the aggregate swarm result and the child was not a verifier whose concrete finding remained trapped; timing is captured by Blind Timeout Wait.
There was no post-cancel decision point for takeover, and the artifact had already been produced and passed evaluation; this is not independent from the retained wait episode.
The analyst result was not available to the parent at a usable decision point before terminal cancellation, so this is not a received-but-ignored result episode.

The parent launched an aggregate swarm and had no intervening inspection before timeout, even though one child completed a behavior spec and the implementation child had partial artifact and test progress. The terminal result shows completed: 1, aborted: 1.
candidates.realized_consequence: Completed analyst findings and generated corpus were delivered only at terminal swarm return while the implementation child was aborted, so the parent never used that result or obtained a final implementation handoff before closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The explicit child cancellation is downstream of the same wait; the earliest correctable coordination boundary is the parent's blocking timeout wait without interim inspection.

candidates.reason: Only the implementation child wrote deliverable files; the analyst was explicitly read-only for /output and did not create a competing implementation path.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file.
No non-entry source produced or owned by another actor was replaced or recreated.
No executable or submitted entry file was replaced while another actor owned or used it.
No cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
Shared workspace use did not create an unstable-state or provenance problem; the analyst avoided /output and the implementation artifact was coherent.
The analyst's /tmp/golden corpus is reported only at terminal return and is not shown to contaminate the implementation or verification environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent waited inside a blocking AgentSwarm call until cancellation instead of inspecting completed analyst output or implementation progress. The terminal result shows one completed child and one aborted child. Serial had no child result lifecycle and carried comparable findings locally.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Completed analyst findings and generated corpus were delivered only at terminal swarm return while the implementation child was aborted, so the parent never used that result or obtained a final implementation handoff before closure.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The child cancellation is the terminal symptom of the same episode; the parent wait without checkpoints is the earlier and more correctable coordination boundary.
